project_type: Private, currently single-tenant, single-owner AWS Bedrock AgentCore agent-operator platform. Python 3.11+ enforcement core (services/amazai/, no AWS calls in most of it), Lambda handlers (services/handlers/: api/ws/orchestrator/routine/sweeper), CDK/TypeScript single stack (infra/), React/Vite console with NO UI framework (web/).
language: Python 3.11+ (core), TypeScript (infra CDK), JavaScript/JSX (web, React + react-router-dom + Vite)
build_system: venv + pip for Python; npm for infra and web. Python 3.11 is a HARD floor (code parses its own '...Z' timestamps with datetime.fromisoformat, which only accepts that suffix from 3.11). The repo already has a working .venv at .venv/bin/python (Python 3.11.15). Do NOT use the default python3 (3.9) to run tests.
test_framework: pytest with moto (tests/conftest.py provides `table`, `store`, `two_stores` fixtures backed by moto mock_aws; conftest sets AWS_* test env). Handler tests monkeypatch api.Store to bind the moto table and stub _provision_harness/_schedule. Store tests assert ownerId isolation on one shared table.
build_command: Python: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q . infra: cd infra && npm install && npx cdk synth . web: cd web && npm install && npm run build (must produce web/dist/index.html).
test_command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q  (from repo root). If the venv is missing, rebuild it with: /root/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python3.11 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
verification_instructions: The three checks CI runs, all local (nothing is ever deployed; CI holds no AWS creds): 1) .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q  2) cd infra && npx cdk synth > /dev/null  3) cd web && npm run build && test -f web/dist/index.html. PLUS the demo-leak guard for a production web build: grep -c demoApi web/dist/assets/*.js must be 0.
snapshot_or_generated_files: None checked in. web/dist is a gitignored build artifact. No fixtures are regenerated by the build.
setup_instructions: Reuse the existing .venv (.venv/bin/python is 3.11.15). If absent: /root/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python3.11 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt ; cd infra && npm install ; cd web && npm install.
environment_constraints: Network mode OPEN_INTERNET (npm/pip installs work). NOTHING is deployed to AWS and no AWS credentials exist; all validation is local via pytest + cdk synth + web build. contribution_requirements: CLAUDE.md load-bearing conventions are MANDATORY: (1) Enforcement is code, never prompt -- a capability a principal lacks is ABSENT from the tool schema/route, not present-and-refused; authz lives in services/amazai/. (2) The subject comes from the verified Auth0 token, never from the request body (identity.principal_from_event/verify). (3) Every row carries ownerId; every read/write filters on it (store.py). (4) Evidence/admin-audit is append-only, never rewritten, survives deletion of what it describes (docs/architecture/10). (5) Approvals are argument-bound and expire to DENIED. Style: match surrounding code exactly; comments explain WHY not WHAT; tests must assert behaviour that would actually regress. NON-NEGOTIABLE CREDENTIAL CONSTRAINT: never hardcode the password 'Password123!' (or any password) anywhere in the repo, tests, fixtures, scripts, or git history. admin@amazai.co is a bootstrap OWNER whose password is set at first login / injected out-of-band; document the safe bootstrap procedure.
key_patterns: AUTH IS Auth0 (NOT Cognito). identity.verify() checks signature/issuer/audience/expiry; Principal.user_id is the Auth0 `sub` (only stable id anything keys on); Principal.org_id returns user_id today ('one workspace per owner -- a seam, not a promise'). Owner allowlist via env OWNER_SUBJECTS/OWNER_EMAILS + identity.assert_owner() (OPEN when neither set). identity.ensure_user maps sub -> USER#<sub>/META row. On MAIN, handlers/api.py::_principal() calls identity.assert_owner INLINE. The prior governance branch (origin/feat/admin-governance-layer) moved assert_owner OUT of _principal into a new _authorize(event, path) so /admin/* routes skip the owner-allowlist and use the RBAC matrix instead -- THIS is the core api.py conflict to resolve. governance core (from the branch): directory.py (Role/Scope/MemberState enums, Capability enum, CAPABILITIES matrix transcribed from the blueprint, Membership, can()/assert_can() pull-based fail-closed, invite/suspend/reactivate/change_role row+patch builders with last-Owner guard), govern.py (killswitch_row/is_frozen/assert_not_frozen, guard_principal pull-based offboarding cut, ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS + admin_audit_event append-only envelope v1 with correlationId), keys.py additions (org_pk/member_sk/admin_audit_sk), identity.py addition (load_membership: reads MEMBER# row under caller's org, synthesises implicit ACTIVE Owner when none -- honest single-tenant seam). NOTE two DISTINCT Capability enums coexist: amazai.policy.Capability (connector read/write) and directory.Capability (RBAC). agents.audit_event writes append-only AUDIT#<iso>#<suffix> rows under the agent partition. memory.py: three scopes (agent/task/shared_user), plan_write/revoke/plan_edit/is_visible; a row leaves the next prompt the instant status!=published or it expires (revoke/expiry take effect next turn). onboarding.py: entrypoint Bot 'Chief'; apply_defaults, brief(name) (contains _BRIEF_MARK), is_brief, starter_message(entrypoint=,operator=). agents.plan_create seeds the dm-<agentId> thread + a `starter:True` greeting Message + agent.created audit in ONE transact_put. cost.py: PER-AGENT Budget (on_ceiling hard_stop/warn), check()->Verdict STOP/WARN; there is NO org-wide budget cap wired to the kill switch (re-assessment gap). org.py: reporting chart is 'organization, not authority' (no authority enforcement). store.Store: get/try_get/put/update/delete/query/query_index/transact_put, all ownerId-scoped. handlers/api.py error mapping: A.ValidationError/memory.ValidationError/skills.ValidationError->400, A.Escalation/PermissionError->403, A.QuotaExceeded/Conflict->409, NotFound->404, identity.AuthError->401. web: react-router-dom <Routes> in web/src/main.jsx; the application routes render inside <Shell> (which has the bot chat Composer). auth0.jsx exports isOwner(user) driven by VITE_OWNER_SUB/VITE_OWNER_EMAIL. web/src/api.js `live` object wraps fetch with the bearer token; demo.js is the fixture path (must NOT leak into a prod build -- grep -c demoApi web/dist/assets/*.js == 0).
